The maximum strain on the V2O5 film was **about 1.6-1.7% in-plane tensile strain**, with a **c-direction compressive strain of about 0.5%**. The paper describes this as "elastic prestrains of <2%" (Muralidharan et al., *ACS Nano* 2017, p. 1, abstract).

- **Derived from substrate strain:** The NiTi substrate was strained to 5% and 10%. With a Poisson ratio of 0.3, the 10% substrate strain gives the largest film strain, about 1.7% in-plane and about -0.5% out-of-plane (Figure 2c, p. 2 of the PDF). The text states an in-plane tensile strain of 1.6% for a c-direction compressive strain of 0.5% (p. 3 of the PDF).
- **Electrochemical samples:** The strained films used for electrochemistry were at -0.35% and -0.5% c-strain (p. 4 of the PDF).
- **Correlated with potential shift:** The paper cites a measured potential shift of about 40 mV at about 1.66% in-plane prestrain (p. 5 of the PDF).
- **DFT modeling:** Simulations applied in-plane strains up to ±2% (Figure 4d caption, p. 4 of the PDF), but these are modeled values, not measured strains on the film.

The XRD-derived strains are averages over the whole coating, so local strains may differ (p. 2 of the PDF).
